answer: Every epoch has a dawn at which the network broadcasts a mesa of truth: a signed summary of who transacted with whom. A new identity may only transact with counterparties whose rows already appear in earlier mesas, so accounts minted together cannot trade with each other to look busy. Each warm-up transaction burns saffron on a decay schedule: the k-th costs k doses, so n heads pay n(n+1)/2 before they can move value. Because the mesa is public and ordered, a cluster that backdates activity is contradicted by the rows it needs, which cannot be pooled or resold.
